title: Santosh Stationary (P) Ltd. v. PuVVNL — CGRF order, Ombudsman under 7.10(iv)
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Arun Tandon, J. and Rekha Dikshit, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed with liberty to approach the Electricity Ombudsman under Clause 7.10(iv).
headnote: A consumer aggrieved by an order of the Electricity Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum—including a finding that the complaint is not covered by Clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005—must pursue the statutory alternative remedy of approaching the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10(iv). The writ was dismissed with liberty to approach the Ombudsman within four weeks; the Ombudsman was to decide the grievance on merits preferably within eight weeks.
facts: M/s Santosh Stationary Private Limited, a consumer of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam, approached the Electricity Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. The Forum recorded that the complaint was not covered within the four corners of Clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Dissatisfied with that finding, the petitioner filed this writ petition in the Allahabad High Court challenging the Forum's order.

holding_units.topic: Ombudsman as statutory remedy against CGRF order
holding_units.holding: If a consumer is aggrieved by a decision of the Electricity Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum, including a finding that the complaint is not covered within Clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the statutory alternative remedy is to approach the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10(iv). A writ against the Forum order was dismissed with liberty to approach the Ombudsman within four weeks; the Ombudsman was directed to decide the grievance on merits preferably within eight weeks of receipt.

principle_tags.application: Even after the CGRF held the complaint outside Clause 7.10, the Court refused writ examination and relegated the consumer to the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10(iv).
